title: Your heart vs. one feather
idea: Siren-style myth, our taste: the weighing of the heart. A monster eats a stranger's heart; Chip's own heart is next on the gold scale against one feather; he lies to the judges, his heart snitches, Spud slaps on the beetle charm (the afterlife's cheat sheet), Chip passes, and the jackal calls Spud's heart next.

hook.what: a little potato beside a giant gold scale in a torch-lit hall, a heart against a feather, a monster waiting; the narrator: In ancient Egypt, one lie could get your heart eaten

captions.text: In ancient Egypt, one *lie* could get your heart eaten.
Heavier than that feather, she eats it. And you're gone. Forever.
Okay. How do I make it light?
Forty-two judges. One question each. Say no to every one.
It's a witness. It saw everything.
A cheat sheet. They buried people with this on their chest. It tells your heart: don't speak against me.
Thousands of those beetles are in museums today. Everyone cheated.
He let him steal the fries.
Wait... why is *YOUR* heart on a scale?

the pan sinks almost to the floor, the monster's breath on the heart

a museum glass case full of green beetle charms
the jackal points: next; now Spud's own heart sits on the pan
